answer: Picture an agent economy as a busy wharf where every ship must pass a random inspection. When an identity is challenged, a jury is drawn by lottery and each juror stakes coins on the verdict — a thread of money tying their judgment to the truth. A willow bends but does not break: honest jurors are paid from the loser's stake, while a Sybil farmer who must corrupt a fresh random jury for every fake identity faces a cost that grows with each attempt, until flooding the harbor costs more than it can ever earn.
